name: Melon
grown_as: A tender annual grown in a greenhouse or cold frame, trained up strings or let to trail. William grows 'Blenheim Orange' (AG 92): a cantaloupe-type melon with netted skin and orange flesh.
habit: A trailing or climbing vine 1.5 to 3 m with softly hairy, ridged stems and simple (unbranched) tendrils. Trained up a support under glass or left to sprawl in a frame.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate, one at each joint, with a tendril beside it
leaf.outline: Rounded to kidney-shaped, 8 to 15 cm across, with 3 to 7 shallow, rounded lobes, often hardly lobed at all
leaf.margin: Small, shallow teeth all round, often wavy
leaf.veins: Palmate, five main veins from the stalk top
leaf.surface: Softly to roughly hairy, slightly wrinkled between the veins

flower.form: A small open yellow star or shallow bell
flower.petals: Five, joined at the base, rounded to bluntly pointed, spreading
flower.centre: Small yellow stamens (male) or a short three-lobed stigma (female)
flower.behind: Five narrow green sepals; the female flower sits on a small hairy oval ovary, the young melon
flower.carried: In the leaf joins: males in small clusters, females singly on the side shoots

fruit: Round, 10 to 15 cm, on a short stalk; skin pale green ripening yellow-green to buff, often with faint ribs and a fine raised net. Ripe fruit smells sweet and cracks around the stalk. Under glass the fruit hang in nets on the support. Seeds narrow, flat, cream, 8 to 12 mm, like cucumber seeds and about the same size or a little larger.
seedling: Two smooth oval seed leaves with rounded tips; first true leaf small, rounded and hairy with shallow lobes.
winter: Nothing: killed by cold and cleared

leaf: a rounded or kidney-shaped leaf with shallow blunt lobes
bloom: for a female, a small hairy oval swelling behind it
seed: pointed oval, about the size of a cucumber seed or a little larger
young: a young vine of a few rounded, shallowly lobed leaves
simple coiling tendrils at the joints
flower: small yellow star flowers at the leaf joints
rounded leaves and tendrils on a trained or trailing vine
crop: round melons on short stalks, skin yellow-green with a fine net

look_alikes: Cucumber leaves are more triangular with sharper, angular lobes. Courgette and squash leaves are much larger and flowers far bigger.
checked: Written 16 November 2026 by Claude from field-guide knowledge. ⚠️ CHECK Seed size corrected on 17 November 2026 (veg redraw, second pass): it said smaller than a cucumber's; melon seeds are usually about the same size or a little larger (8 to 12 mm).
